text: Let $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$ be any points on the curves $(x-1)^{2}+(y+1)^{2}=1$ and $y=x^{2}$, respectively. The distance between $P$ and $Q$ is minimum for some value of the  abscissa of $P$ in the interval :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The circle has centre $C(1,-1)$ and radius 1. The least distance between the circle and the parabola is along a normal to the parabola that passes through $C$: if $Q$ is its foot on $y=x^{2}$, then $P$ is the point of segment $CQ$ at distance 1 from $C$.

The normal to $y=x^{2}$ at $Q(t,t^{2})$ has slope $m=-\dfrac{1}{2t}$:

$y-t^{2}=-\dfrac{1}{2t}(x-t)$

It passes through $(1,-1)$:

$-1-t^{2}=-\dfrac{1-t}{2t}\Rightarrow 2t^{3}+3t-1=0$

$g(t)=2t^{3}+3t-1$ is increasing, with $g(0.3)=-0.046<0$ and $g(0.32)=0.026>0$, so $t\in (0.3,0.32)$ and $|m|=\dfrac{1}{2t}\in (1.56,1.67)$. Then $Q\approx (0.31,0.10)$ and $CQ\approx 1.30>1$, so the curves do not meet.

From $C$, the point $Q$ lies up and to the left along the normal, so

$x_{P}=1-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+m^{2}}}$

With $1+m^{2}\in (3.44,3.78)$, $\sqrt{1+m^{2}}\in (1.85,1.95)$, so $x_{P}\in (0.46,0.49)$, about $0.47$, which lies in $\left (\dfrac{1}{4},\dfrac{1}{2}\right )$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text: If the maximum value of $a$, for which the function $f_{a}(x)=\tan ^{-1}2x-3ax+7$ is non-decreasing in $\left (-\frac{π}{6},\frac{π}{6}\right )$, is $\bar{a}$, then $f_{\bar{a}}\left (\frac{π}{8}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\text{Given,}$

$\begin{array}{ll} f_{a}(x) & =\tan ^{-1}2x-3ax+7 \\  \\ f_{a}^{'}(x) & =\dfrac{2}{1+4x^{2}}-3a \end{array}$

As the function $f_{a}(x)$ is non-decreasing

$\begin{array}{l} \text{in}\left (-\dfrac{π}{6},\dfrac{π}{6}\right ), \\  \\ f_{a}^{'}(x)\geq 0 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \dfrac{2}{1+4x^{2}}-3a\geq 0\Rightarrow \dfrac{2}{1+4x^{2}}\geq 3a \\  \\ \Rightarrow a\leq \dfrac{2}{3(1+4x^{2})},\text{when}x\in \left (-\dfrac{π}{6},\dfrac{π}{6}\right ) \\  \\ \because a\text{is maximum when}x^{2}=\dfrac{π^{2}}{36}, \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll} a_{\max } & =\dfrac{2}{3\left (1+\frac{4π^{2}}{36}\right )}=\dfrac{2\times 12}{36+4π^{2}} \\  \\ \qquad =\dfrac{6}{9+π^{2}} \\  \\ \therefore \bar{a} & =\dfrac{6}{9+π^{2}} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore f_{\bar{a}}(x)=\tan ^{-1}2x-\dfrac{18}{9+π^{2}}x+7 \\  \\ f_{\bar{a}}\left (\dfrac{π}{8}\right )=\tan ^{-1}2\left (\dfrac{π}{8}\right )-\dfrac{18}{9+π^{2}}\times \dfrac{π}{8}+7 \\  \\ =\tan ^{-1}\dfrac{π}{4}-\dfrac{9π}{36+4π^{2}}+7 \\  \\ =7+\tan ^{-1}\dfrac{π}{4}-\dfrac{9π}{4(9+π^{2})}\approx 7.29 \end{array}$

This value matches none of the options. NTA dropped this question in its final answer key, so it is treated as a bonus question.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text: Let $β=\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{αx-\left (e^{3x}-1\right )}{αx(e^{3x}-1)}$ for some $α\in \mathrm{ℝ}$. Then the value of $α+β$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$β=\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{αx-(e^{3x}-1)}{αx(e^{3x}-1)},α\in R$

$=\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{\frac{α}{3}-\left (\frac{e3x-1}{3x}\right )}{αx\left (\frac{e3x-1}{3x}\right )}$

So, $α=3$ (to make indeterminate form)

$β=\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{1-\left (\frac{e3x-1}{3x}\right )}{3x}=\frac{1-\frac{\left (3x+\dfrac{9x2}{2}+......\right )}{3x}}{3x}$

$=\frac{-\left (\frac{9}{2}x^{2}+\frac{(3x)3}{3!}+....\right )}{9x^{2}}=\frac{-1}{2}$

$\therefore$ $α+β=3-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{5}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text: The value of $\log _{e}2\frac{d}{dx}(\log _{\cos x}\mathrm{cosec}x)$ at $x=\frac{π}{4}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $f(x)=\log _{\cos x}\mathrm{cosec}x=\dfrac{\ln \mathrm{cosec}x}{\ln \cos x}=-\dfrac{\ln \sin x}{\ln \cos x}$.

By the quotient rule:

$f^{'}(x)=-\dfrac{\cot x\qquad \ln \cos x-\ln \sin x(-\tan x)}{(\ln \cos x)^{2}}=-\dfrac{\cot x\qquad \ln \cos x+\tan x\ln \sin x}{(\ln \cos x)^{2}}$

At $x=\dfrac{π}{4}$: $\cot x=\tan x=1$ and $\ln \cos x=\ln \sin x=\ln \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\ln 2$.

$f^{'}\left (\dfrac{π}{4}\right )=-\dfrac{-\frac{1}{2}\ln 2-\frac{1}{2}\ln 2}{\frac{1}{4}(\ln 2)^{2}}=\dfrac{\ln 2}{\frac{1}{4}(\ln 2)^{2}}=\dfrac{4}{\ln 2}$

Therefore $\log _{e}2\cdot f^{'}\left (\dfrac{π}{4}\right )=\ln 2\cdot \dfrac{4}{\ln 2}=4$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

$=20\int\limits _{0}^{π}(1+|\sin 2x|)dx$

text: Let the solution curve $y=f(x)$ of the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{xy}{x^{2}-1}=\frac{x^{4}+2x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}$, $x\in (-1,1)$  pass through the origin. Then $\int\limits _{-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}f(x)dx$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{xy}{x^{2}-1}=\frac{x^{4}+2x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}$

which is first order linear differential equation.

Integrating factor $(I.F.)=e^{\int \frac{x}{x2-1}dx}$

$=e^{\frac{1}{2}\ln |x^{2}-1|}=\sqrt{|x^{2}-1|}$

$=\sqrt{1-x^{2}}$

$\because$ $x\in (-1,1)$

Solution of differential equation

$y\sqrt{1-x^{2}}=\int (x^{4}+2x)dx=\frac{x^{5}}{5}+x^{2}+c$

Curve is passing through origin, $c=0$

$y=\frac{x^{5}+5x^{2}}{5\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}$

$\int\limits _{\frac{-\sqrt{3}}{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}\frac{x^{5}+5x^{2}}{5\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}dx=0+2\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}\frac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}dx$

put $x=\sin θ$

$dx=\cos θdθ$

$I=2\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{3}}\frac{\sin ^{2}θ.\cos θdθ}{\cos θ}$

$=\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{3}}(1-\cos 2θ)dθ$

$=\left (θ-\frac{\sin 2θ}{2}\right )\left |_{0}^{\frac{π}{3}} \right.$

$=\frac{π}{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text: Let the abscissae of the two points $P$ and $Q$ on a circle be the roots of $x^{2}-4x-6=0$ and the ordinates of $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$ be the roots of $y^{2}+2y-7=0$. If $\mathrm{PQ}$ is a diameter of the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}+2ax+2by+c=0$, then the value of $(a+b-c)$ is $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Abscissae of PQ are roots of $x^{2}-4x-6=0$

Ordinates of PQ are roots of $y^{2}+2y-7=0$

and PQ is diameter

$\Rightarrow$ Equation of circle is

$x^{2}+y^{2}-4x+2y-13=0$

But, given $x^{2}+y^{2}+2ax+2by+c=0$

By comparison $a=-2,b=1,c=-13$

$\Rightarrow a+b-c=-2+1+13=12$

text: If the line $x-1=0$ is a directrix of the hyperbola $kx^{2}-y^{2}=6$, then the hyperbola passes through the point :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given hyperbola : $\frac{x^{2}}{6/k}-\frac{y^{2}}{6}=1$

Eccentricity $=e=\sqrt{1+\frac{6}{6/k}}=\sqrt{1+k}$

Directrices : $x=\pm \frac{a}{e}\Rightarrow x=\pm \frac{\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{k}\sqrt{k+1}}$

As given : $\frac{\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{k}\sqrt{k+1}}=1$

$\Rightarrow k=2$

Here hyperbola is $\frac{x^{2}}{3}-\frac{y^{2}}{6}=1$

Checking the option gives $\left (\sqrt{5},-2\right )$ satisfies it.

text: If $0<x<\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $\frac{\sin ^{-1}x}{α}=\frac{\cos ^{-1}x}{β}$, then the value of $\sin \left (\frac{2πα}{α+β}\right )$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $\frac{\sin ^{-1}x}{α}=\frac{\cos ^{-1}x}{β}=k\Rightarrow \sin ^{-1}x+\cos ^{-1}x=k(α+β)$

$\Rightarrow α+β=\frac{π}{2k}$

Now, $\frac{2πα}{α+β}=\frac{2πα}{\frac{π}{2k}}=4kα=4\sin ^{-1}x$

Here $\sin \left (\frac{2πα}{α+β}\right )=\sin (4\sin ^{-1}x)$

Let $\sin ^{-1}x=θ$

$\because$ $x\in \left (0,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )\Rightarrow θ\in \left (0,\frac{π}{4}\right )$

$\Rightarrow x=\sin θ$

$\Rightarrow \cos θ=\sqrt{1-x^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \sin 2θ=2x.\sqrt{1-x^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \cos 2θ=\sqrt{1-4x^{2}(1-x^{2})}=\sqrt{(2x^{2}-1)^{2}}=1-2x^{2}$

$\because$ $\left (\cos 2θ>0\mathrm{as}2θ\in \left (0,\frac{π}{2}\right )\right )$

$\Rightarrow \sin 4θ=2.2x\sqrt{1-x^{2}}(1-2x^{2})$

$=4x\sqrt{1-x^{2}}(1-2x^{2})$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text: The integral $\int \frac{\left (1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )(\cos x-\sin x)}{\left (1+\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\sin 2x\right )}dx$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\cos x-\sin x=\sqrt{2}\sin \left (\dfrac{π}{4}-x\right )$ and

$1+\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\sin 2x=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\left (\sin \frac{π}{3}+\sin 2x\right )=\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}}\sin \left (x+\frac{π}{6}\right )\cos \left (\frac{π}{6}-x\right )$

The constant becomes $\left (1-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )\sqrt{2}\times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}-1}{2\sqrt{2}}=\sin \dfrac{π}{12}$, so the integrand is

$\frac{\sin \frac{π}{12}\sin \left (\frac{π}{4}-x\right )}{\sin \left (x+\frac{π}{6}\right )\cos \left (\frac{π}{6}-x\right )}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{\cos \left (\frac{π}{6}-x\right )-\cos \left (\frac{π}{3}-x\right )}{\sin \left (x+\frac{π}{6}\right )\cos \left (\frac{π}{6}-x\right )}$

Since $\cos \left (\dfrac{π}{3}-x\right )=\sin \left (x+\dfrac{π}{6}\right )$ and $\cos \left (\dfrac{π}{6}-x\right )=\sin \left (x+\dfrac{π}{3}\right )$, the integrand equals $\dfrac{1}{2}\left [\mathrm{cosec}\left (x+\dfrac{π}{6}\right )-\mathrm{cosec}\left (x+\dfrac{π}{3}\right )\right ]$.

With $\int \mathrm{cosec}θdθ=\ln \left |\tan \dfrac{θ}{2}\right |$:

$I=\frac{1}{2}\ln \left |\tan \left (\frac{x}{2}+\frac{π}{12}\right )\right |-\frac{1}{2}\ln \left |\tan \left (\frac{x}{2}+\frac{π}{6}\right )\right |+C=\frac{1}{2}\log _{e}\left |\frac{\tan \left (\frac{x}{2}+\frac{π}{12}\right )}{\tan \left (\frac{x}{2}+\frac{π}{6}\right )}\right |+C$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text: Let $A=\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7\}$ and $B=\{3,6,7,9\}$. Then the number of elements in the set $\{C\subseteq A:C\cap B\neq 𝜙\}$ is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As C $\cap$ B $\neq$ $𝜙$, C must not be formed only by {1, 2, 4, 5}

$\therefore$ Number of subsets of $A = 2^{7} = 128$

and number of subsets formed by {1, 2, 4, 5} = 16

$\therefore$ Required no. of subsets $= 2^{7}$ $-$ $2^{4} = 128$ $-$ 16 = 112

text: Suppose $y=y(x)$ be the solution curve to the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}-y=2-e^{-x}$ such that $\lim _{x\to \infty }y(x)$ is finite. If $a$ and $b$ are respectively the $x$ - and $y$-intercepts of  the tangent to the curve at $x=0$, then the value of $a-4b$ is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
IF $=e^{-x}$

$y~.\quad e^{-x}=-2e^{-x}+\frac{e^{-2x}}{2}+C$

$\Rightarrow y=-2+\frac{e^{-x}}{2}+Ce^{x}$

$\lim _{x\to \infty }y(x)$ is finite so $C=0$

$y=-2+\frac{e^{-x}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{e^{-x}}{2}\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}\left |_{x=0}=-\frac{1}{2} \right.$

Equation of tangent

$y+\frac{3}{2}=-\frac{1}{2}(x-0)$

or $x+2y=-3$

So $a=-3,b=-\frac{3}{2}$

$\Rightarrow a-4b=3$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text: The number of matrices $A=\left (\begin{array}{ll} a & b \\ c & d \end{array}\right )$, where $a,b,c,d\in \{-1,0,1,2,3,\ldots \ldots ,10\}$, such that $A=A^{-1}$, is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A=A^{-1}$ means $A^{2}=I$:

$A^{2}=\left (\begin{array}{ll} a^{2}+bc & b(a+d) \\ c(a+d) & d^{2}+bc \end{array}\right )=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right )$

If $a+d\neq 0$, then $b=c=0$ and $a^{2}=d^{2}=1$ with $a=d$, giving $a=d=1$ or $a=d=-1$: 2 matrices.

If $a+d=0$, then $d=-a$ must also lie in $\{-1,0,1,\ldots ,10\}$, so $a\in \{-1,0,1\}$, and $a^{2}+bc=1$.

For $a=d=0$: $bc=1$, so $(b,c)=(1,1)$ or $(-1,-1)$: 2 matrices.

For $(a,d)=(1,-1)$ or $(-1,1)$: $bc=0$, and with 12 values available for each entry the pairs with $b=0$ or $c=0$ number $12+12-1=23$, giving $2\times 23=46$ matrices.

Total $=2+2+46=50$.

Hence, the answer is 50.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift
